programs.name: YLRL Ethel Smith K4LMB Memorial Scholarship
programs.summary: $2,500 for a licensed female amateur radio operator seeking a Bachelor's or Graduate degree full time at an accredited college or university. There are no residency restrictions and non-US amateurs are eligible. YLRL membership and a communications, radio or electronics course of study are both preferences, not bars.

deadline.note: The captured page publishes no opening date and no deadline anywhere. It describes the three scholarships and points at the YLRL apply page for the current opening and deadline dates. Deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed.

constraints.rawText: Applicant must be female.
Applicant must have an Amateur Radio License. There are no residency restrictions. Non-U.S. Amateurs are eligible.

The Ethel Smith, K4LMB and Mary Lou Brown, NM7N scholarships are intended for full-time students. For these scholarships, applicants must intend to seek a Bachelor's or Graduate degree from an accredited college or university.
Preference will be given to students studying communications, radio, electronics, or Amateur Radio related arts and sciences.

programs.name: YLRL Marte Wessel K0EPE Memorial Scholarship
programs.summary: $1,500 for a licensed female amateur radio operator studying part time at an accredited educational institution while working full time. Stay-at-home parents and caregivers count as full-time work, and high-school students are exempt from the work requirement. Any accredited technical or vocational school and any two- or four-year college qualifies. YLRL restricts neither enrolment intensity nor degree level, so a degree level it does not list is one it never named rather than one that fails to qualify.

deadline.note: The captured page publishes no opening date and no deadline anywhere. It points at the YLRL apply page for the current opening and deadline dates. Deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed.

programs.name: Yasme Foundation Supporting Grants
programs.summary: Board-selected support for youth programmes, developing-country radio societies, Reverse Beacon Network nodes and other foundations' scholarship funds; the companion Yasme Excellence Award is recognition on the same board-initiated basis. Observed awards run $5,000 to $7,500. There is no application form, no portal and no deadline.

deadline.note: There is no application and no deadline. The board initiates awards and announces them retrospectively, roughly twice a year. The practical route is to be visible: publish your work and let the board find it.

constraints.rawText: Awards are board-initiated. There is no application process.

programs.name: NCDXF Grant Program
programs.summary: Cash grants to individuals and groups who use amateur radio to advance education, science and international goodwill. NCDXF states no amount, no cap and no total; its guidelines distinguish only "major support" for expeditions to the most-wanted locations from "a smaller amount of support" for other projects. In practice the recipients are well-designed DXpeditions to locations high on the most-wanted lists, so this is not a collegiate programme. Applicants must have a significant financial stake of their own.

deadline.note: Rolling: the guidelines page publishes no deadline of any kind. NCDXF's own instruction is to allow lead time, because the entire Board of Directors reviews each application — normally you should allow two months lead time for action.

programs.applyContact: Applications must be made by completing (1) a Budget Worksheet and (2) an Application Form, and submitting both to NCDXF.

constraints.rawText: A basic philosophy of the NCDXF is that expedition participants themselves should have a significant financial stake in their expedition and that the expedition should be likely to proceed even without financial support from the NCDXF.

spec.note: The applicant must carry a significant financial stake; NCDXF does not fund the whole cost.

constraints.rawText: The Northern California DX Foundation (NCDXF) is a US non-profit organization which provides financial support to individuals and groups who use amateur radio communications to advance and promote education, science and international goodwill.

spec.note: The project must advance education, science or international goodwill through amateur radio.

constraints.rawText: The NCDXF encourages applicants to be active financial contributors to the Foundation.

spec.note: Being an active financial contributor to NCDXF is encouraged.

fundingRestrictions: With the exception of excess baggage charges, we do not consider commercially available transportation costs when we are working on a grant request approval.

Expeditions to unusual locations as defined by the Islands on the Air (IOTA) program, Grid Square awards and various radio contests are not supported unless the support can be justified without reference to these activities.

costShareRequired.quote: A basic philosophy of the NCDXF is that expedition participants themselves should have a significant financial stake in their expedition and that the expedition should be likely to proceed even without financial support from the NCDXF.

programs.rawOtherText: Applications must be made by completing (1) a Budget Worksheet and (2) an Application Form, and submitting both to NCDXF. Please include all the information requested on the worksheet and form. This will speed the review of your application.

programs.name: NCDXF W6EEN Memorial Scholarship
programs.summary: Full tuition at any DX University or Contest University session held in North America, for licensed amateurs aged 25 or younger. "There is no restriction as to class of license" means any class qualifies, not that a licence is unnecessary — the same sentence begins "If you are a licensed amateur radio operator". No dollar figure is published because the award is the course itself, and an eligible ham applies by contacting the university directly rather than NCDXF.

amount.amountRaw: Full tuition at DX University or Contest University sessions held in North America.

deadline.note: No deadline is published. Availability tracks the DX University and Contest University session schedules, which NCDXF does not restate on this page.

constraints.rawText: If you are a licensed amateur radio operator 25 years of age or younger, you can apply for a free tuition scholarship by contacting the appropriate University directly.
There is no restriction as to class of license.

programs.summary: A youth grant listed by NCDXF whose page renders as navigation and a title only: it publishes no terms, no amount and no deadline. Recorded so that somebody searching for it learns that, rather than assuming GrantSpotter missed it.

deadline.note: No terms of any kind are published on the page. Contact NCDXF directly if you need this one.

programs.name: SARA Student and Teacher Project Grants
programs.summary: The Society of Amateur Radio Astronomers funds student radio-astronomy projects in several small grants of no more than $200 each, or more with the approval of the grant committee — a ceiling with discretion above it rather than a stated maximum. The award is cash, not a kit: Radio JOVE, SuperSID and INSPIRE are named only as projects an applicant might build with the money. Fifth grade through college is SARA's word "Preference", not a bar. Teachers are eligible too.

amount.amountRaw: The funds will be divided up into several small grants of no more than $200 each or more, with the approval of the grant committee, to ensure that the money reaches the largest number of students.

deadline.note: Rolling. No deadline of any kind appears anywhere on the grants page.

programs.applyContact: Email the completed form to grants at radio-astronomy.org

constraints.rawText: Preference will be given to students 5th grade through college and to new and innovative ideas.
UPDATE: Teachers are now eligible to apply for grants to bring radio astronomy to the classroom.

spec.note: Teachers became eligible by a later update line on the same page.

programs.name: Radio Club of America Scholarship Program
programs.summary: Sixteen named funds, the Rappaport, Carr and Cooper awards among them, for undergraduate and graduate students on a wireless career track. An amateur licence is NOT required. RCA publishes no per-award amount; about $15,000 a year is distributed in total. Only students at roughly nine participating schools are eligible and the university selects the recipients, so a student never applies to RCA: the action is to ask your department whether your school participates.

deadline.note: No deadline is published. Awards are distributed each May, and the timeline is set by the participating university rather than by RCA. If your school participates, ask your department for its internal date.

constraints.rawText: Only students at roughly nine participating schools are eligible, and the university selects the recipients. Students do not apply to the Radio Club of America directly.

spec.note: The institution nominates; no student-facing application exists.

constraints.rawText: Undergraduate and graduate students on a wireless career track. A ham licence is NOT required.
